```{r matrix algebra}
my_matrix = matrix(c(5, 6, 4, 1, 8, 4), nrow = 2, 
       ncol = 3, byrow = TRUE)
my_matrix 

secondmatrix = matrix(4,2,2)
secondmatrix

R1 = matrix(c(4,-2,3,5), nrow=2,ncol=2)
R1

R2 = matrix(c(0,6,3,1), nrow=2,ncol=2)
R2

# addition of matrices R1 and R2
sum = R1 + R2
sum

# subtraction
difference = R1 - R2
difference

# multiplication
product = R1*R2
product

# division ## this is NOT CORRECT - NOT MATRIX ALGEBRA
result = R1/R2
result
########
R3 <- matrix(c(10,20,20,40), 
             ncol = 2, 
             byrow = TRUE)
R3
# Equivalent to:
rankMatrix(R3)[1] # number of rows or columns -which ever is minimum fewer 
#rank = [columns or rows (which ever is less  )] - 1
#kinda like degrees of freedom 

#diagonal matrix
diagmatrix = diag(c(22,-14,56))

diagmatrix
#determinant of a matrix
R4 <- matrix(c(3,9,7,2),
             ncol = 2, 
             byrow = TRUE)
R4
det(R4)


#inverse of a matrix
R5 <- matrix(c(19,11,2,33),
             ncol = 2, 
             byrow = TRUE)
solve(R5)

#transpose of a matrix
R6 <- matrix(c(19,11,2,33),
             ncol = 2,
             byrow = TRUE)
t(R6)

##Eigenvalues and Eigenvectors
#eigenvalues and eigenvectors both are calculated by using eigen() function. The eigenvalues are stored on the 
#'values' of the list and by default it will display the decreasing order.
#Syntax: eigen(matrix name) $values 
#For eigenvectors, they are stored in 'vectors' of the list. 
#Syntax: eigen(matrix name) $ vectors . 

R7 <- matrix(c(19,11,2,33), 
             ncol = 2,
             byrow = TRUE)

# show the eigen values of matrix R7
eigen(R7)$values

# show the eigen vectors of matrix R7
eigen(R7)$vectors 

#The matrix must be square for the calculation of power. 
#Since there is no built-in function to calculate the power of the matrix. 
#So, we can use any two of the methods, i.e., '%^%' operator of the 'expm' package and the' matrix.power' function of the 'matrixcalc' package. 


R8 <- matrix(c(19,11,2,33),
             ncol = 2, 
             byrow = TRUE)
R8^2 ##dont use this!

R8*t(R8) ##USE THIS
```
```{r regression}
#Regression Example

#matrix of X (indicators) and constant

M1 <- matrix(c(1,2,1,1,3,5,1,5,3,1,7,6,1,8,7), nrow = 5, 
       ncol = 3, byrow = TRUE)

#transpose of indicator matrix
M1
t(M1)

#create transpose - another way
TransM1 <- t(M1)
TransM1

#Y observed criterion matrix - 
Y1 = matrix(c(3,2,4,5,8), nrow=5,ncol=1)
Y1

# Multiplication of transpose of predictors by predictors
TransM1%*%M1
TransXbyX <- TransM1%*%M1
TransXbyX

# product of transpose of X and Y

TranxXY <- TransM1%*%Y1
TranxXY

# inverse of the Tranpose of X - solve() produces inverse
InvXTranX <- solve(TransXbyX)
InvXTranX

# product of the inverse of X transpose X by the Transpose of X by Y
# gives us the regression coefficients in order of 
# the constant, B1 and B2
InvXTranX%*%TranxXY

```
